To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amplitude of single event transient current is related to the input voltage and the shape of current waveform does not obey the classical exponential model.
the amplitude of current pulses in a CMOS amplifier circuit is dependent on the input voltage.
the transient current pulse is dependent of the input voltage and the transient current wave forms do not obey the double exponential model when the LET is high enough.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of single event transients induced by heavy ions.
modeling and analysis of analog circuits for SEU and SET.
the analysis of the single event transients (SET) and their impact on circuit performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single event transients are strongly affected by the input voltage, the LET of the particle, and the biasing of the device.
the single event transient is depending on the circuit and device design.
the transient currents are not only dependent on the LET of the incident particle but also on the circuit input voltages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transient current and voltage in the circuit are depending on the circuit input and output voltages and also on the LET of the incident particle.
the current and voltage waveform of the amplifier circuit are not only dependent on the circuit parameters but also on the particle incident energy.
, the current pulse is a function of the input voltage and the LET.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use TCAD tools to simulate the single event transients and the results are very close to the real measurements.
it is possible to predict the transient waveforms and their amplitude using circuit and device-level simulations.
the transient current waveform in the amplifier circuit can be modeled by the double exponential model when the input voltage is lower than the threshold voltage of the transistor.
